Terms of Reference for the Horizon Scandal Inquiry:

1. The inquiry will establish the facts about the faulty Horizon IT system and its impact on subpostmasters, including:
a. Understanding and acknowledging what went wrong and key lessons that must be learned.
b. Obtaining all available relevant evidence from the Post Office, Fujitsu, BEIS and other relevant organizations.
2. The inquiry will consider the following matters:
a. The role of the Post Office, Fujitsu and other relevant organizations in the development, implementation and management of the Horizon IT system.
b. The adequacy of the investigations conducted by the Post Office and others into the Horizon IT system and related issues.
c. The impact of the Horizon IT system on subpostmasters, including financial losses, reputational damage and personal consequences.
d. The effectiveness of the complaints process and any legal action taken by subpostmasters.
e. The response of the Post Office, Fujitsu and other relevant organizations to the issues raised by subpostmasters.
f. The steps taken to address the failings of the Horizon IT system and to support subpostmasters.
3. The inquiry will make recommendations to ensure that a scandal like this does not happen again, including:
a. The Horizon Compensation Advisory Board (HCAB) should not be prevented from monitoring individual cases.
b. HCAB shall produce written reports in respect of each of their meetings.
c. Membership of HCAB should be increased to ensure that it has sufficient capacity.
d. The government should within 28 days seek directions under section 5 of the Inquiries Act 2005 to enable the inquiry to compel the production of evidence from the Post Office, Fujitsu and other relevant organizations.
4. The inquiry will be independent and transparent, with regular updates provided to those affected and the wider public.
5. The inquiry will be chaired by a person with relevant experience and expertise, who will be appointed by the Secretary of State for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy (BEIS).
6. The inquiry will have the power to appoint experts, specialists and counsel to support its work.
7. The inquiry will publish its final report
